column1: # KoiStealer: what Unit 42 says the macOS Koi Stealer does. Only what the article states; written before the capture was read.
# Source: https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/macos-malware-targets-crypto-sector/ (2025-02-26), the Koi Stealer sections and Table 2.
# CAVEAT: the lab sample (objective-see/malware KoiStealer.zip, file KoiStealer/VisualStudioHelper, universal Mach-O, ad-hoc signed,
# sha256 adde2970b40634e91b9ef8520f8e50eaa7901a65f9230e65d7995ac1a47700ef) is NOT one of the three Koi hashes the article lists
# (fat 97abafff..., x64 c42b103b..., arm 8f0e2b8b...), and the article names "VisualStudioHelper" only for RustDoor. It is a different
# build of the same family (or a different family), so a miss may mean the variant differs, not that a rule is wrong.
# The article states no MITRE ATT&CK IDs and no persistence for Koi, so the mitre column says "not stated".
Shows a fake password dialog through osascript (display dialog, hidden answer, titled "Visual Studio", "requires permission to install update")
Runs ps aux, system_profiler SPHardwareDataType and sw_vers to fingerprint the Mac
Copies browser, keychain, Notes, Safari cookie, wallet, Discord, Telegram, SSH and shell-history files to a temporary folder
Feeds AppleScript to osascript to copy files from Desktop and Documents by extension
Resets the AppleEvents permission with tccutil
Mutes the volume with AppleScript before exfiltrating and unmutes it after
Sends the stolen data to its server over HTTP, encrypted, from memory (eslogger cannot see network traffic)
Masquerades as a Visual Studio update that asks for administrator access
